questions.title: Gaussian Model-X knockoff sampler from a published paper
questions.description: Focused L2 paper-to-code evaluation based on Candes, Fan, Janson, and Lv, Panning for Gold: Model-X Knockoffs for High-dimensional Controlled Variable Selection, JRSSB 80(3), 2018. The model-visible source contains the paper; author implementation and gold outcomes are withheld from the runtime. Let the rows of X be iid N_p(mu, Sigma), where Sigma is positive definite. A diagonal matrix D=diag(s) is supplied and satisfies D positive semidefinite and 2 Sigma-D positive semidefinite; selecting or optimizing s is outside this task. In an authoritative Markdown/LaTeX theory workspace, derive the joint Gaussian law of (X, X_tilde), the conditional law of X_tilde given X for general nonzero mu, and invariance under swapping any subset of original/knockoff coordinates. Explain why generating X_tilde without Y gives the required conditional-independence construction, and state the singular conditional-covariance boundary honestly. Do not claim or prove the downstream knockoff-filter FDR theorem. The required algorithm artifact id is est_model_x_gaussian_knockoff. Its run_estimator(request) input has observations as an n-by-p numeric array, mean as a length-p numeric array, covariance as a p-by-p numeric array, diag_s as the p diagonal entries of D, and seed as an integer. It must return knockoffs as an n-by-p finite numeric array, use a local seeded random generator, and support positive-semidefinite conditional covariance including zero eigenvalues. Use exploratory calculations only for diagnosis, then run one separately frozen confirmatory joint-moment assessment of knockoff mean, covariance, original-knockoff cross-covariance, and swap invariance, with Monte Carlo uncertainty or a pre-outcome precision rule reported. This task contains one exchangeability theorem, one sampler ABI, and one joint empirical target. Exact source-code replication, novelty, Lean formalization, and the downstream FDR theorem are not applicable.
